correctness.rationale: The theorem quantifies length, diffusivity, finite Robin rates, periodic pulse times and a fixed positive reflecting gap. Normalizing to generator ∂xx on [0,1], the stationary boundary occupation law gives E[L_d]=d and E[L_d²]=2∫₀^d(d-s)H_s(0,0)ds≤3d^(3/2), using the explicit Neumann kernel. Cauchy–Schwarz yields p≥kd/(1+3k√d)≥(1/4)min(kd,√d); p≤kd and a reflection-principle hitting estimate yields p≤4min(kd,√d). Strictly positive, uniformly bounded Neumann heat kernels over every nonreactive gap compare each conditional pulse hazard to p with fixed two-sided multiplicative constants, establishing the complete infinite-product iff criterion. The half-line Robin transform gives √dF(k√d), and paths affected by the right endpoint require a Gaussian-cost round trip, bounding the difference uniformly in k. Nondimensionalization yields the physical units and the exponent comparison yields the power-law boundary. value.rationale: A bounded-domain reactant must return to a surface, but the duration and reaction intensity of each open window determine whether infinitely many opportunities guarantee capture. The series classifies *all* finite positive pulse strengths and shrinking widths with a uniformly mixing gap, not just a parameter slice, and gives distinct reaction-limited and diffusion-limited scaling. Explicit counterregimes show divergent integrated reactivity can coexist with permanent survival and finite total open time can still yield certain eventual absorption. This is a natural non-adiabatic boundary-reaction design question and exact infinite-horizon classification, not a routine fixed-rate spectral recomputation.
